dataset_family: SMG-SNU Boramae Medical Center and Dongjak-Gu Center for Dementia, Seoul, 2012-2020: an amnestic MCI clinical cohort distinct from Korea University Guro (P-643)
method_family: Two-step cluster analysis of NPI-Q-derived MBI domains coded present/absent, with Cox survival analysis of progression to AD and FreeSurfer vertex-wise cortical thickness comparison (MRI subset n = 202). The Cox survival component is the same method family as P-647's survival analysis.
what_it_shows: The sample is 1,184 aMCI patients followed for 3.1 years on average, of whom 284 progressed to AD. The affective-dysregulation-only cluster (NPI-Q depression and/or anxiety; SGDS 7.8 versus 4.5) did not carry a significantly higher adjusted hazard of AD than the asymptomatic cluster (HR 1.214 [0.883-1.670], p = 0.232). It showed no cortical thinning against that cluster; its right superior temporal cortex was thicker. A post-hoc contrast of affective patients with SGDS > 6 against asymptomatic patients without significant depressive symptoms was also null (HR 1.237, p = 0.266). BUT the continuous SGDS score predicted progression in univariate Cox (HR 1.040 per point [1.007-1.075], p = 0.017), and converters had higher baseline SGDS (6.5 versus 6.0, p = 0.038). Presence of the affective-dysregulation domain also predicted progression after adjustment (HR 1.373, p = 0.021).
why: PARTLY, and internally divided. For the row's severity clause: aMCI patients whose only symptoms were affective, with clearly higher SGDS, had no significantly higher adjusted AD hazard and no cortical thinning against asymptomatic patients. The authors' SGDS > 6 contrast was also null, and they conclude that 'the severity of depressive symptoms was not associated with the risk of AD'. Those contrasts are presence or profile contrasts, however, not grading of severity within depressed patients: the MBI domains were coded 'without considering the severity and frequency', and the SGDS > 6 contrast compares depressed with non-depressed patients. AGAINST the row: its specific claim is that within the supporting studies 'continuous severity scores fail to track ... conversion'. P-989's own continuous severity score DID track conversion in univariate Cox (HR 1.040 per SGDS point, p = 0.017; converters 6.5 versus stable 6.0, p = 0.038). The multivariable SGDS coefficient is not reported. On that limb the study sits with P-26, not with the supporters, so it cannot be a clean supporter of the continuous-score clause. The finder's note omitted this result. OTHER LIMITS: the first clause is not tested, since all participants are aMCI. The cortical-thickness subset is small (55, 47 and 100 patients), SGDS was a covariate of no interest in the vertex-wise model, and no SGDS-thickness correlation is reported. MBI was approximated from a 1-month NPI-Q window, and there are no amyloid or tau biomarkers. INDEPENDENCE: the site (Boramae/Dongjak-Gu) and authors (Yoon, Lee, Kwak, Kim) differ from P-643's Korea University Guro group (Hyung, Kang, ... Jeong) and from every other supporter and candidate. The survival-analysis method overlaps P-647.

quotes.quote: Age (hazard ratio (HR) [95% confidence interval (CI)] = 1.097 (1.074–1.121), p < 0.001), years of education (HR [95% CI] = 0.963 (0.938–0.989), p = 0.005), MMSE (HR [95% CI] = 0.885 (0.857–0.914, p < 0.001) and SGDS scores (HR [95% CI] = 1.040 (1.007–1.075), p = 0.017) were significantly associated with the risk of progression to AD in univariate Cox regression analyses, and were used as covariates in the following Cox multivariate regression analyses.

Compared with the asymptomatic group (reference group), the complex group revealed a higher risk of progression to AD (HR [95% CI] = 2.541 [1.904–3.392], p < 0.001), but the affective dysregulation group did not (HR [95% CI] = 1.214 [0.883–1.670], p = 0.232) (Figure 1).

There were no significant differences in cortical thickness between the asymptomatic group and the complex group. While, the affective dysregulation group showed thicker cortex in right superior temporal gyrus than the asymptomatic group (Figure 2B; Table 6). In subcortical structures, there were no differences between 3 groups.

The affective dyregulation group with significant depressive symptoms did not reveal higher risk of progression to AD (HR = 1.237 [0.850–1.798], p = 0.266) compared with the asymptomatic group without significant depressive symptoms (n = 326, 58.1%). These findings suggest that the severity of depressive symptoms was not associated with the risk of AD in our study participants.
In the present study, MBI domains were approximated using the NPI-Q without considering the severity and frequency.
